title: 8 alternatives to swag at conferences

# 8 alternatives to swag at conferences


By Izabelle Hundrev


●


5 min. read


●


Nov 17, 2026


[Marketing](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/category/marketing/)


Branded swag has been a staple at conferences and trade shows for years. But it comes with downsides: much of it is[mass-produced from cheap materials](https://chhs.source.colostate.edu/lanyard-to-landfill-swag-should-evolve-or-die-csu-professor-says/) and doesn’t last.


Even decent quality swag may not stick around long. In a 2025 survey,[88% of marketers reported having thrown away swag immediately after receiving it](https://www.getmobly.com/post/state-of-swag-2025) .


Below, you’ll find eight alternatives to traditional conference swag with examples and tips to help you find the right fit for your audience, goals, and budget.


## Key takeaways


-


**Traditional branded swag isn't the only way to engage event attendees.** Alternatives include snacks, digital rewards, experiences, services, and charitable donations.


-


**Match your giveaway to your event goals.** Snacks and on-site services can attract foot traffic, while prize drawings and rewards for attending demos can help generate leads.


-


**Plan around your audience and budget.** Small, broadly appealing giveaways work well for reaching a large crowd, while exclusive experiences are better suited to building relationships with priority prospects.


-


**Prioritize convenience.** Digital and experiential rewards, like subscriptions and onsite services, eliminate the need to carry anything home. If you’re offering physical rewards, ensure they’re lightweight and carry-on friendly.


## 8 swag alternatives your event attendees will appreciate


From practical items to memorable experiences, these eight ideas offer different ways to engage attendees at your next event.


## 1. Digital gift cards and payouts


Digital rewards are a convenient alternative to physical swag, especially for attendees visiting from out of town. This can include[digital gift cards](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/digital-vs-physical-gift-cards/) , prepaid cards, and monetary payouts like PayPal or Venmo.


For example, you could offer booth visitors a $10 coffee or rideshare gift card they can use right away, or a larger monetary reward for participating in a product demo or completing a survey. To give recipients more choice, consider using an[incentive platform](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/incentive-platforms-digital-payouts/) that offers multiple reward options so each person can pick what they prefer.

## 2. Travel-friendly snacks and beverages


A snack or beverage is a practical option for attendees who spend long days in sessions or are traveling home. It gives people a reason to stop by your booth, and it won’t take up much space in their luggage.


Individually packaged items that fit in a carry-on are easy to grab and go. Think locally-made chocolate, granola bars, or single-serve coffee, tea, or electrolyte packets.


If you want to keep your brand top of mind, many snack vendors offer custom packaging. Make sure to label common allergens and include at least one gluten-free or vegan option for attendees with dietary restrictions. It’s also worth checking the venue’s food and beverage policies before you order, since some limit what exhibitors can hand out.


## 3. Prize drawings and sweepstakes


A prize drawing or[sweepstakes](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/how-to-run-an-effective-sweepstakes/) gives booth visitors a chance to win one larger prize. Entry typically requires scanning a badge or filling out a short form with contact information.


When choosing a prize, look for something with broad appeal that’s easy to receive, like a $500 digital gift card or a popular tech gadget shipped directly to the winner. Announcing the winner at a set time near the end of the event can encourage people to return to your booth.


A single grand prize often costs less than giving away smaller items to every person who stops by. This option also lets you collect leads for post-event follow-up. Just be clear about how you’ll use their information, and keep marketing opt-ins separate from the entry itself.


## 4. Digital subscriptions


A free month or two of a digital subscription gives attendees something to enjoy long after the event ends.


Look for subscriptions that align with your audience’s interests, like an audiobook service, an online learning platform, or a mindfulness app. Choose an option that doesn’t auto-renew or require card details, so attendees don’t receive an unexpected charge when the gift period ends.


Since most subscriptions are delivered as codes, they’re also easy to send to virtual or hybrid event participants.


## 5. Gifts from a local small business


Give attendees a taste of the host city with gifts from a local small business. This could be coffee from a neighborhood roaster, specialty foods, or small items from independent artisans, like postcards or stickers.


Prioritize items that are lightweight and distinctive to the host city. Gift cards to nearby restaurants are another great option, since attendees can use them for dinner during the conference. Reach out to vendors several weeks ahead to confirm quantities and arrange pickup or delivery, since small businesses might not keep large inventories on hand.


Sourcing gifts locally supports the community hosting the event and gives attendees a more personal memento of their trip.


## 6. Experiences


Instead of a physical or digital gift, invite attendees to share an experience. Host a dinner, take a small group to a local sporting event, or organize a beverage-tasting class. Invite your highest-value customers and prospects a few weeks before the event, then fill any remaining spots with attendees you connect with onsite. Keep the group small and require RSVPs to manage headcount.


A shared experience gives your team more time with prospects than a quick booth conversation does, making it easier to build stronger relationships. Guests also have a chance to network with each other.


## 7. Onsite booth services


Turn your booth into a place attendees want to visit by offering a useful on-the-spot service.


Professional headshots are one option, since many attendees might want an updated photo for LinkedIn or their company website. Hire a photographer for the day, and collect email addresses so you can send each person their photos after the event. Other ideas include a phone charging station, chair massages, or a barista serving specialty drinks.


Booth services can attract foot traffic and give your team time to talk with visitors while they wait. Following up with headshots or a thank-you note also gives a natural reason to reconnect after the show.


## 8. Charitable donations


Donations give attendees a reason to engage with your brand while supporting a good cause.


For example, you could donate a set amount for every booth visitor or badge scan. Consider partnering with a local nonprofit or allowing visitors to choose which cause their donation supports. After the event, share the final donation total with everyone who participated.


Cybersecurity company Armis[replaced its trade show swag with a program called “Scan For A Cause,”](https://www.armis.com/blog/why-armis-has-replaced-corporate-swag-at-global-trade-shows-with-charitable-giving/) which made a charitable donation for every badge scanned. Armis reported that the program led to more meaningful engagement at its booth than traditional swag.


## Choosing the right swag alternative for your next event


The best booth giveaway depends on your audience, budget, and goals. Snacks and onsite services are great for attracting foot traffic, while prize drawings and digital rewards help you capture leads. If your goal is building relationships, a hosted experience might be a better fit.


Consider your audience’s interests and how many people you want to reach. A small reward for hundreds of visitors calls for a different budget than an exclusive experience for a limited group of prospects.


Whatever you choose, make it something useful or meaningful. A thoughtful giveaway can leave a stronger impression of your brand than another water bottle with your logo on it.
